summary: Citizens of the other CEMAC states (Cameroon, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea, Chad and the Central African Republic) enter the Republic of the Congo freely. The Congolese embassy in Washington and the UK, Canadian and German governments say their citizens need a visa arranged in advance; no official source we could read states the rule for most other nationalities.

payments.text: The Government of Canada says the economy is primarily cash-based. Major hotels and stores generally accept major credit cards, euros and US dollars (confirm when you book), but outside these establishments in Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire credit cards are rarely accepted.

safety.text: The UK FCDO reports opportunistic crime such as pickpocketing, particularly in Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire, and says criminals may target foreigners and vehicles, especially outside urban centres and in the Pool Region and Mouyondzi District. It says no live conflict has been reported in the Pool Region since a 2017 ceasefire, but violent clashes could arise again with little notice. It advises against all travel within 50 km of the border with the Central African Republic in Likouala, against walking in the streets after dark, and to carry a colour copy of your passport and visa entry stamp, as police may ask for ID.

tips.text: Do not confuse the Republic of the Congo (Brazzaville) with the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Kinshasa) across the river: they are separate countries, each with its own visa.
The UK FCDO says you must have certificates proving yellow fever and polio vaccination to pass border control.

Always carry identification: the UK FCDO advises a colour copy of your passport including the visa entry stamp, and the Government of Canada says you may be detained if you cannot produce acceptable identification.
The Government of Canada says the economy is primarily cash-based and that, outside major hotels and stores in Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire, credit cards are rarely accepted.

The Government of Canada says it is illegal to photograph government buildings, military installations, border crossings and transport infrastructure, including ports, train stations and airports. It advises seeking permission before photographing official buildings or individuals.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for the Republic of the Congo?
faq.answer: CEMAC citizens (Cameroon, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea, Chad and the Central African Republic) enter freely, and Rwandans get a free visa on arrival. US, British, Canadian and German citizens need a visa obtained in advance, according to the Congolese embassy in Washington and those governments' travel advice. No official source we could read states the rule for most other nationalities, and none describes an electronic visa.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Congo-Brazzaville?
faq.answer: Rwandan ordinary-passport holders get a free visa on arrival for up to 90 days under a bilateral agreement. The Congolese embassy in Washington says no Congolese visa is issued at any port of entry, and Canada's and Germany's travel advice say the same for their citizens.

faq.question: Is this the same country as the DRC?
faq.answer: No. The Republic of the Congo (capital Brazzaville) and the Democratic Republic of the Congo (capital Kinshasa) are different countries facing each other across the Congo River, each with its own visa. A visa for one is not valid for the other.

faq.question: Is yellow fever vaccination required for the Republic of the Congo?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK's travel advice says you must have a yellow fever vaccination certificate to pass border control.

faq.question: Is the Republic of the Congo safe to visit?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO advises against all travel within 50 km of the border with the Central African Republic in Likouala Region, and warns that clashes could break out with little notice in parts of the Pool region. It reports opportunistic crime such as pickpocketing, particularly in Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire, and advises against walking after dark.
